context_requirements: Expression of the thiazide-sensitive NaCl cotransporter SLC12A3 (NCC), which is absent or negligible in the nine profiled cell lines
An intact distal nephron tubular epithelium with WNK-SPAK/OSR1 kinase signaling, absent in these lines
Functional carbonic anhydrase and KCNQ1 channel activity in a renal transport context; not sufficient in these lines
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in the 978 landmark genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Induction of a coherent transcriptional program (e.g., cell-cycle, stress, or transport gene sets) shared across multiple lines
Evidence of thiazide-sensitive ion transport or NCC-dependent signaling in these lines

evidence.supports: Thiazide use in humans was associated with only a single modest gene-expression difference (CCL14) in peripheral blood, indicating minimal direct transcriptional impact.

Meticrane, a thiazide diuretic, altered viability and transcription in leukemia and liver cancer lines, but the changes were in non-cancer pathways and not clearly attributable to the thiazide mechanism.
Compensatory transcriptional responses to thiazide-sensitive NCC loss occur in kidney distal nephron cells, a context absent from the nine profiled cell lines.
